episodes.title: Should Christians Play GTA 6?
episodes.description:
GTA 6 is here, and millions of people are taking time off work to play it. In this Ask Away! Live Q&A, Brandon Anderson and Joshua Garner talk about how much a Christian's faith should shape the games, shows and movies they choose. Brandon gives two questions to ask about any media: does it help you become more like Christ, and does it glorify what God hates? We look at Romans 1 and what it means to approve of sin from behind a screen, when a game becomes an idol, whether Roblox is safe for kids, and why calling in sick to play is lying. Video games aren't sinful in themselves, but every hobby belongs on the altar.

episodes.title: Why I Am a Protestant   Yet I Will Rejoice
episodes.description:
Catholic, Orthodox, or Protestant: what separates the three branches of Christianity, and why does it matter? In this episode, Brandon Anderson explains why he is unashamedly a Protestant. Starting with Martin Luther and the Reformation, he walks through the five solas: Scripture alone, grace alone, faith alone, Christ alone, and to the glory of God alone. Along the way he looks at why Scripture is the final authority over tradition and the Pope (2 Timothy 3–4), why no indulgence, pilgrimage, or work can earn salvation (Ephesians 2), how the thief on the cross was saved by faith without ever being baptized (Luke 23), and why Jesus' sacrifice on the cross was sufficient once for all. Brandon also shares why he believes there are true followers of Jesus in all three branches, and why these five truths still shape his life today.

episodes.title: Should Christians Trust AI With Their Questions?
episodes.description:
More people, especially teenagers, now take their hardest questions to AI before they ever ask a pastor. In this Ask Away! Live Q&A, Brandon Anderson and Joshua Garner talk about why that matters. AI can gather information and arrange it into knowledge, but wisdom begins with the fear of the Lord, and a machine can't fear God. We talk about AI's counterfeit humility, why it tends to tell us what we want to hear (2 Timothy 4), how the Holy Spirit gifts believers to serve one another (1 Peter 4), and why pastors can bear fruit in a way AI never can (Matthew 7). AI is a useful tool, and Christians have no reason to fear it, because Jesus is Lord over all of it.

episodes.title: How should Christians view the death penalty?
Why did Jesus have to die?
episodes.meta: Why did Jesus have to die? Sin deserves death, the penalty had to be paid, and Jesus took it on our behalf. A Bible-based answer from Brandon Anderson.
episodes.summary:
Jesus had to die because God is consistent, holy and just: sin is rebellion against Him, the penalty for sin is death, and that penalty has to be paid. Brandon explains the wages of sin (Romans 6:23), why Scripture ties forgiveness to the shedding of blood (Hebrews 9:22), and how Jesus, who lived without sin, took the punishment in our place so that believers receive His righteousness.

The resurrection proved that Jesus is who He claimed to be. Brandon closes with a story of two brothers to picture what substitution means.
key_points: God doesn't change, so His righteous judgment against sin is consistent (Hebrews 13:8).
Sin is anything we think, say or do that is contrary to God's nature, and its wages is death (Romans 6:23).
No amount of good deeds can cancel wrongdoing, just as past kindness doesn't erase a murder at trial.
Without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness (Hebrews 9:22); Jesus' sinless life made Him the suitable sacrifice.
God showed His love by sending Christ to die for us while we were still sinners (Romans 5:8, John 3:16).
The resurrection proves who Jesus is and shows He conquered both sin and death.
This gift is received by faith in Jesus (2 Corinthians 5:21).
episodes.description:
This is a question that many Christians have asked throughout the life of the Christian Church. So what does the Bible say in regards to this question? In this episode, Brandon will seek to answer that question based on what scripture says, and why it was necessary for Jesus to die.

4:36 Judgment for Our Works
6:35 Jesus Took Our Punishment
9:28 The Story of the Two Brothers
12:32 The Only Way, and Closing

episodes.title: What does it mean to be created in the image of God?
How do I read the Bible?
How can I know that I am a Christian?
Is it important for Christians to go to church?
How should I respond to the election as a Christian?
Are Mormons and Jehovah's Witnesses Christians?
How do I share the Gospel?
What is the Gospel?
episodes.meta: What is the gospel? The good news that God did what we couldn't: Jesus lived, died and rose so we can be right with God by faith.
episodes.summary:
The gospel means "good news," and at its core it is this: God did what we couldn't. Brandon walks from creation and humanity's rebellion through the Old Testament promises of a Messiah to Jesus, who lived a sinless life, took the punishment for our sin on the cross and rose again.

Salvation is a gift received by faith, not something earned by good works (Ephesians 2:8), and it is good news meant to be shared with everyone.
key_points: "Gospel" simply means good news: what Jesus Christ has done to make a way for us to be right with God.
God created everything good. Humanity rebelled, and sin and death entered the world.
Even our best efforts can't repair the relationship (Isaiah 64:6), because God requires perfection.
The Old Testament promised a Messiah who would descend from Abraham, be a prophet like Moses, reign as David's king and bear our punishment (Isaiah 53).
Jesus, fully God and fully man, lived sinlessly, died in our place and rose again.
Salvation comes by grace through faith, as a free gift (Ephesians 2:8).
episodes.description:
The word “Gospel” is thrown around a lot today. But what does it really mean? How does Jesus and the Bible fit into the Gospel? Here Brandon answers the question of what is the Gospel, and why it matters to you!

4:14 God's Promise of a Chosen One
6:17 A King From David's Line
8:45 Jesus Christ, the Messiah
11:09 The Cross and Resurrection
12:59 Telling the World, and Closing

episodes.title: What does it mean to be a Christian?
Is Jesus God?
episodes.description: Not only does the Bible claim Jesus was the Messiah and a prophet, but it also says Jesus is God. In today’s episode, Brandon discusses how Jesus claimed to be God and what people today believe about Him. Is He a liar, is He a lunatic, or is He Lord?

episodes.title: If God is good, why do bad things happen?
episodes.meta: If God is good, why do bad things happen? Brandon answers from Scripture: a broken world, no one righteous on their own, and a patient God who sent Jesus.
episodes.summary:
Bad things happen because we live in a broken world, not because God is absent or unkind. Brandon opens with compassion for anyone going through something hard right now, then explains that God made the world good, that humanity's rebellion brought sin and death, and that Scripture says no one is righteous on their own (Romans 3).

He argues God's goodness shows in sending Jesus, in joining us in our brokenness, and in patiently delaying judgment so more people can come to know Him.
key_points: The brokenness we see in relationships, health and finances traces back to the fall, not to God's original design (Genesis 1–3).
Scripture says no one is righteous on their own (Romans 3:10–12, 23), which changes the question "why do bad things happen to good people?"
Even our good works are like filthy rags before a perfect God (Isaiah 64:6).
God's goodness shows in sending Jesus: the wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life (Romans 6:23).
Jesus joined us in this broken world and sympathizes with our weakness (Hebrews 4:15, John 1:14).
God is also just and will one day destroy all evil; His patience in the meantime lets more people come to faith.
episodes.description:
Brandon answers one of the most-asked questions to Christians: Why does God allow bad things to happen to good people?

We've all wondered why good things happen to bad people. So why exactly does it happen? If God is so good, why does He let it happen?

Whether you've been a Christian for a long time or you barely know the name “Jesus” this question comes up in life almost daily. So let's dive in and find out how the Bible answers this tough question!

8:10 God's Rich Mercy and Grace
9:10 God Joined Us in Our Brokenness

episodes.title: What is the Bible?
episodes.meta: What is the Bible? One story of redemption written by 40+ authors over 1,500 years. How it is organized, why Christians trust it, and where to start.
episodes.summary:
The Bible is a collection of writings by more than 40 authors across about 1,500 years, written in Hebrew, Greek and a little Aramaic, that tells one unified story of God's plan to redeem humanity. Brandon explains why Christians believe it is inspired and preserved by God (2 Timothy 3:16, 2 Peter 1:20–21) and traces that story from creation and the fall through the promises about the Messiah to Jesus and the gospel.

He also lays out how the Old and New Testaments are organized and suggests that new readers begin with the Gospel of Luke.
key_points: The Bible is not just one book: it was written by 40+ real people with real lives, over roughly 1,500 years, in three languages.
Christians believe Scripture was inspired by God and preserved by His Spirit (2 Timothy 3:16; 2 Peter 1:20–21).
Its unified story: God created everything good, humanity rebelled, and God made a way back through Jesus.
Old Testament genres: law, history, poetry, and the major and minor prophets. New Testament: the Gospels, Acts, Paul's letters, other letters and prophecy.
The Bible isn't arranged strictly in chronological order.
If you're new to reading it, start with the Gospels, perhaps Luke, which pairs with the book of Acts.
